paper.title: Influenza Vaccination Among Individuals With Type 1 Diabetes in Denmark: Coverage, Persistence, and Determinants, 2015-2022
paper.code_data_availability: Data Availability Statement: 'The data that support the findings of this study are available from Statistics Denmark. …

registers.role: outcomes: annual influenza vaccination status for each season, and the covariate 'vaccination in the previous season'
sample frame, linkage and controls: personal identification number, sex, date of birth, region of residence, residence and vital status
variables_mentioned: region of residence (Capital Region of Denmark/Central Denmark Region/North Denmark Region/Region Zealand/Region of Southern Denmark)

registers.name_in_paper: Register of Laboratory Results for Research
registers.role: controls: latest HbA1c measurement before each season
controls: hospital admissions for severe hypoglycaemia and ketoacidosis before season start; hospital diagnosis of T1D feeding the diabetes classifier
variables_mentioned: ICD-10 diagnosis codes (listed in Table S1)

registers.role: controls: highest attained education level (parents' for ages 1-18)

variables_mentioned: employment status (employed incl. students / unemployed / retired)

linkages: All registry records are linked using the mandatory personal identification number assigned to all Danish citizens at birth or immigration.
For individuals aged 1-18, employment status and education are the parents' highest employment status and highest completed education in years (Table 1 footnotes a and b).
Each individual contributes one person-year observation per influenza season in which they meet the inclusion criteria; vaccination status is also linked to the individual's previous season.

sample.universe: All Danish citizens diagnosed with type 1 diabetes, aged 1-64 years and residing in Denmark from 1 October 2015 to 1 July 2022 (the entire nationwide population meeting the eligibility criteria; no a priori sample size calculation)
sample.unit_of_observation: person-season (person-year): one observation per individual per eligible influenza season, each season running 1 October to 30 September of the following year
selection_rules: Diagnosed with type 1 diabetes (Open-Source Diabetes Classifier) on or before 1 October of the season
Alive and resident in Denmark on 1 October of the season

Aged 1-64 years at season start; individuals > 65 years excluded to minimise confounding from overlapping vaccination incentives (they are eligible for free vaccination regardless of chronic conditions)
Individuals diagnosed with T1D between 1 October 2014 and 30 September 2015 excluded
Each individual's first season after diagnosis from 1 October 2015 onward excluded, to ensure availability of previous-season vaccination data and avoid bias related to timing of diagnosis
Stratified into 1-18 years (paediatric) and 19-64 years (adult) by age at season start
Observations with values still missing after last-observation-carried-forward imputation excluded (Figure S2)
sample.period: influenza seasons 2015/16 to 2022/23 (each 1 October to 30 September)

construction_notes: Date of diabetes diagnosis obtained with the Open-Source Diabetes Classifier, a validated algorithm combining HbA1c measurements, hospital diagnosis of T1D, diabetes-specific visits at the podiatrist, and purchases of glucose lowering drugs [14].
Age and diabetes duration defined at the start of each season and modelled as categorical variables using quartiles; time-dependent variables reassessed at the start of each season.
HbA1c dichotomised at the Danish Endocrine Society treatment goal: < 53 mmol/mol (in target) vs >= 53 mmol/mol (above target); the latest measurement before each season is used.
Severe hypoglycaemia and ketoacidosis coded 'Yes' if the individual had at least one hospital admission for the condition before the start of the season (ICD-10 codes in Table S1).
Education categorised as 0-10, 11-15 and > 15 years; employment as employed (including students), retired or unemployed; for ages 1-18 the parents' values are used.

Missing values imputed by last observation carried forward (LOCF) in R: 13.1% of HbA1c, 12.6% of employment and 0.09% of education observations were imputed; observations still missing afterwards were excluded.
IVC calculated each season as vaccines administered divided by population size, reported with 95% confidence intervals.
Persistence defined as receipt of influenza vaccination in > 80% of eligible seasons; sensitivity analyses used > 70% and > 85%.
Across both age groups individuals contributed a median of 8 seasons.
Data management and statistical analyses performed in R version 4.3 with packages from CRAN.

claims.statement: Male sex (vs female, reference) is not associated with influenza vaccination coverage among individuals with type 1 diabetes aged 1-18 years in Denmark.

treatment.label: male sex (vs female, reference)

definition.value: Binary indicator for male sex, from the Danish Civil Registration System; female is the reference category in the forest plot.

timing.value: measured at the start of each influenza season (1 October); time-dependent variables were reassessed at the start of each season

outcome.label: influenza vaccination coverage (receipt of influenza vaccination in the season)

definition.value: Annual influenza vaccination status for each influenza season, taken from The Danish Vaccination Registry; IVC is calculated each season as vaccines administered divided by population size. In the regressions the outcome is receipt of influenza vaccination in the person-season, and the adjusted relative risk is >1 for higher vaccination coverage (the forest plot axis is labelled 'Low vaccination coverage' / 'High vaccination coverage').

timing.value: during the influenza season, defined as 1 October to 30 September of the following year

units.value: adjusted relative risk (ratio of the probability of influenza vaccination relative to the reference category)

estimand.target_population: Person-seasons of individuals with type 1 diabetes aged 1-18 years (paediatric population) resident in Denmark across the influenza seasons 2015/16-2022/23
estimand.time_horizon: the influenza season following the covariate measurement at season start

population.description: Person-seasons of individuals with type 1 diabetes aged 1-18 years (paediatric population) resident in Denmark across the influenza seasons 2015/16-2022/23
population.selection: Alive, resident in Denmark and diagnosed with T1D on or before 1 October of the season; individuals diagnosed with T1D between 1 October 2014 and 30 September 2015, and each individual's first season after diagnosis, were excluded; individuals > 65 years were excluded; observations with missing values remaining after LOCF were excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: Observed cross-sectional and between-season variation in demographic, socioeconomic and clinical characteristics among individuals with T1D; there is no reform, lottery, discontinuity or instrument -- the paper reports mutually adjusted associations, not an exogenous shock

key_assumptions.assumption: Poisson regression with robust standard errors, with all covariates entered mutually and age and diabetes duration modelled as quartile categories, correctly describes the probability of influenza vaccination
Clustering at the individual level adequately accounts for the dependence induced by individuals contributing one observation per eligible season
Missing HbA1c, employment and education values are well approximated by the last observation carried forward, because these variables remain relatively stable across influenza seasons
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper reports the imputed shares (13.1% of HbA1c, 12.6% of employment and 0.09% of education observations) and excludes observations still missing after LOCF (Figure S2)

key_assumptions.assumption: Residual confounding from unmeasured factors such as health-seeking behaviour or physician recommendations cannot be excluded (the authors state the association is not interpretable as a causal effect)

implies_edges.to: male sex (vs female, reference)
influenza vaccination coverage (receipt of influenza vaccination in the season)

key_assumptions.assumption: The sample is conditioned on being alive and resident in Denmark with a T1D diagnosis at the start of each season, which the authors note may introduce survivorship bias

implies_edges.to: inclusion in the estimation sample (alive, resident in Denmark and diagnosed with T1D on or before 1 October of the season)

key_assumptions.assumption: Influenza vaccinations are completely and correctly recorded in The Danish Vaccination Registry
key_assumptions.supported_by: Reporting of administered vaccines has been mandatory since November 2015 and 85% of credibility indicators were graded 4 or 5 (Table S10); the authors concede minor misclassification from under-registration of vaccinations administered outside Denmark

threats_discussed: comorbidities and other potential motivators for vaccination were not included in the analyses, which may have led to an overestimation of coverage among individuals with T1D alone
lack of data on health care visits, which may influence vaccination opportunities
no data on vaccination coverage or persistence for other vaccination programmes such as COVID-19 vaccination, which prevents establishing an association between increased IVC and COVID-19 vaccination
residual confounding from unmeasured factors such as health-seeking behaviour or physician recommendations
misclassification of diabetes type, particularly in younger individuals
HbA1c values carried forward may not fully reflect glycaemic control
survivorship bias from requiring survival and residence at the start of each season
under-registration of vaccinations, particularly those administered outside Denmark

definition.value: Employment status from the Employment Classification Module, categorised as employed (including students), retired or unemployed; employed is the reference category. For those aged 1-18 the parents' highest employment status is used.

timing.value: measured at the start of each influenza season (1 October); time-dependent variables were reassessed at the start of each season

outcome.label: influenza vaccination coverage (receipt of influenza vaccination in the season)

definition.value: Annual influenza vaccination status for each influenza season, taken from The Danish Vaccination Registry; IVC is calculated each season as vaccines administered divided by population size. In the regressions the outcome is receipt of influenza vaccination in the person-season, and the adjusted relative risk is >1 for higher vaccination coverage (the forest plot axis is labelled 'Low vaccination coverage' / 'High vaccination coverage').

timing.value: during the influenza season, defined as 1 October to 30 September of the following year

units.value: adjusted relative risk (ratio of the probability of influenza vaccination relative to the reference category)

population.description: Person-seasons of individuals with type 1 diabetes aged 19-64 years (adult population) resident in Denmark across the influenza seasons 2015/16-2022/23
population.selection: Alive, resident in Denmark and diagnosed with T1D on or before 1 October of the season; individuals diagnosed with T1D between 1 October 2014 and 30 September 2015, and each individual's first season after diagnosis, were excluded; individuals > 65 years were excluded; observations with missing values remaining after LOCF were excluded.

identification.source_of_variation: Observed variation in demographic, socioeconomic and clinical characteristics among individuals with T1D; mutually adjusted associations, no exogenous variation

key_assumptions.assumption: Poisson regression with robust standard errors, with all covariates entered mutually and age and diabetes duration modelled as quartile categories, correctly describes the probability of influenza vaccination
Clustering at the individual level adequately accounts for the dependence induced by individuals contributing one observation per eligible season
Missing HbA1c, employment and education values are well approximated by the last observation carried forward, because these variables remain relatively stable across influenza seasons
key_assumptions.supported_by: The paper reports the imputed shares (13.1% of HbA1c, 12.6% of employment and 0.09% of education observations) and excludes observations still missing after LOCF (Figure S2)

key_assumptions.assumption: Residual confounding from unmeasured factors such as health-seeking behaviour or physician recommendations cannot be excluded (the authors state the association is not interpretable as a causal effect)

threats_discussed: comorbidities and other potential motivators for vaccination were not included in the analyses, which may have led to an overestimation of coverage among individuals with T1D alone
lack of data on health care visits, which may influence vaccination opportunities
no data on vaccination coverage or persistence for other vaccination programmes such as COVID-19 vaccination, which prevents establishing an association between increased IVC and COVID-19 vaccination

under-registration of vaccinations, particularly those administered outside Denmark

ambiguities: The article prints no estimate, interval or p-value for any persistence analysis; the direction is taken from the Section 3.4 sentence and the magnitude is left null.

statistically_significant is set true because the paper says the factor 'was associated with' persistence, which elsewhere in the article corresponds to a 95% CI excluding 1.00; the interval itself is in supplementary material not included in the PDF.

The paper reports 'factors associated with' persistence and states that residual confounding cannot be excluded; the graph edge is recorded as tested because the schema has no association-only edge kind.

evidence.how: The paper states that this factor 'was associated with' low (or higher) persistence; throughout the article a factor is called associated when the mutually adjusted 95% confidence interval excludes 1.00, so the claim is recorded as statistically significant. No estimate or interval is printed in the article.

value.claimed_domain: vaccination patterns among Danish individuals with type 1 diabetes
boundary_conditions: generalizability to newly diagnosed or older individuals is limited because the design requires survival and residence at the start of each season
individuals > 65 years, who are eligible for free influenza vaccination regardless of chronic conditions, are excluded from the main analyses
